check.finding: The two sides are not counted the same way. NYC's number is DOE district schools only, excluding roughly 150,000+ charter-school students that Colorado's statewide total does include, and possibly excluding some pre-K enrollment as well. On a consistent definition (all public school students, any type), New York City likely has MORE students than Colorado, not fewer -- the opposite of what the sentence implies.
check.conflict: NYC DOE's own Mayor's Management Report and Wikipedia both confirm charter-school students are counted separately from DOE enrollment (119,551 charter students as of Oct 2018, a figure that has grown substantially since). Colorado's 870,793 figure is a single statewide count that includes charter and pre-K students. Adding NYC's charter enrollment (now well over 150,000) to the 793,300 DOE figure would push NYC's total public-school population past 900,000 -- likely exceeding Colorado's count rather than trailing it.
check.resolution: Reworded to compare the city's district schools with Colorado's whole public system, and the caveat now says counting charters and pre-K would put New York City ahead.

Two minor caveats: FY25 actual is the city's fiscal year that ended mid-2025, so the figure is over a year old at the time of this audit (NYC's own FY26 plan already targets 34,975); and Austria's 'Exekutivbedienstete' is a slightly broader executive-service term than a strict translation of 'police officers,' though it is the term commonly used for Austrian police staffing.

items.sentence: loses as many people to traffic crashes as all of Sweden

nyc.label: Traffic deaths in New York City, 2025
nyc.quote: There were 205 recorded traffic deaths in 2025, a 19 percent decline from 253 fatalities last year

match.label: Road deaths in Sweden, 2025
match.quote: Under 2025 omkom 203 personer i olyckor i vägtrafiken

items.note: Department of Transportation's 2025 Vision Zero year-end release; Trafikanalys (Sweden's official transport statistics agency) release on 2025 road deaths. Ireland (185) is the backup.

check.finding: Both figures are calendar-year 2025 totals of traffic-crash deaths, quoted verbatim, and the ratio (203/205 = 0.9902) matches. The Swedish release separately breaks out and excludes road-related suicides from its 203 figure, keeping the two counts on a comparable accidental-death basis.

items.sentence: holds as many people in jail as Switzerland holds in all its prisons
items.caveat: Fiscal 2025 average; the jail population passed 7,000 later in 2025.

nyc.label: NYC jail average daily population, FY2025
nyc.quote: The average daily population (ADP) in Fiscal 2025 was 6,823, an increase of nearly 10 percent from Fiscal 2024.

items.note: Department of Correction average daily population for fiscal 2025 from the Mayor's Management Report; Switzerland's total prison population at Jan. 31, 2026 per World Prison Brief, citing the Swiss Federal Statistical Office. The Board of Correction's January 2026 report gives a fiscal 2026 year-to-date average of 7,247.

check.finding: The two figures are not measured the same way: NYC's 6,823 is a fiscal-year (July 2024-June 2025) average daily population, while Switzerland's 7,119 is a single-day snapshot from January 31, 2026, about seven months after NYC's measurement window closed. Given DOC's own steadily rising ADP trend (up nearly 10 percent in the latest year alone), NYC's true jail population as of early 2026 is plausibly already close to or above Switzerland's figure, not safely below it as the 1.0434 ratio implies.

items.sentence: makes as many arrests a year as Buffalo has people

An earlier version used a third-party aggregator's Vintage 2024 figure of 276,854; the Bureau's newer estimate has Buffalo shrinking.

check.finding: The NYC side is a solid, live first-party query, but the Buffalo figure comes from a private demographics aggregator rather than the Census Bureau directly, and a newer official Census estimate shows Buffalo's population has since fallen rather than matching the figure used; recomputing with it moves the ratio from 0.9925 to about 0.984.

check.resolution: Re-sourced to the Census Bureau's own Vintage 2025 file, replacing a third-party aggregator; Buffalo's newer estimate is 274,613.
